attempts.label: DANDI:001773
attempts.paper_title: Deep brain stimulation induces white matter remodeling and functional changes to brain-wide networks
attempts.entry_title: White matter remodeling and network changes after SCC-DBS in macaques (Fujimoto et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most main findings hold up in this data: stimulation raised fractional anisotropy in the mid-cingulate bundle, increased myelinating oligodendrocytes with thicker myelin, lowered cortical and raised subcortical connectivity, and reduced subgenual cingulate connectivity with default mode, limbic and executive networks. In the implanted but unstimulated monkey, the opposite fractional anisotropy decrease also reproduced. The nonsurgical controls' lack of change, the local increase at the implant site and the network-sorted connectivity plot could not be tested, because whole-brain maps, control seed data and ROI names are missing. The connectivity results assume the deposited maps are those the paper analysed. One minor claim failed: that monkey's foraging fell, and the paper reports no test for it.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Fujimoto, Fujimoto, Elorette et al. (2026) on dandiset 001773, which holds the paper's derived values (voxel FA, voxel seed connectivity, group connectomes, CC1 and DAPI counts, EM g-ratios, home-cage behavior bins) and its MATLAB scripts. It repeats the paper's ANOVAs, Tukey-Kramer tests and rank-sum tests for the stimulated monkeys N and T, the lead-implanted monkey D and the nonsurgical controls. The whole-brain voxel maps and the controls' seed connectivity are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fujimoto et al. (2026) from dandiset 001773

outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the FigE1 script's model (monkey, condition and their interaction), condition gives F(1,236) = 34.61, P = 1.4e-08, partial eta squared 0.128 for movement and F(1,236) = 17.35, P = 4.4e-05, 0.068 for foraging. Reading (b) gives F 33.81 and 16.46, both P below 1e-04. The post probability is higher in N (movement 0.083 to 0.550, foraging 0.033 to 0.050) and in T (0.200 to 0.383, 0.017 to 0.300).
deviations: The foraging values are read as 1 yes and 0 no, as for movement; the sheet's legend says yes 2 and no 1, which no value uses.

outcomes.notes: By the criterion's test, a one-way ANOVA of monkey D's 120 bins on condition, movement does not differ (0.383 pre, 0.267 post, F(1,118) = 1.86, P = 0.175) but foraging does (11 of 60 bins before, 3 of 60 after, 0.183 to 0.050, F(1,118) = 5.32, P = 0.023; Fisher exact P = 0.043). The paper reports no test for monkey D (its Extended Data Fig. 1 legend analyses only N and T), so the test is the claims file's reading of the Methods applied to one animal. The deposited FigE1 script (135 lines) runs its only test calls, anovan (lines 18 and 19) and multcompare (24 and 26), on the rows of group 1 (N and T); monkey D's rows (monkey 3, group 2) enter only the means, standard errors and sample sizes of lines 35 to 125. The deposited script therefore runs no test for monkey D. The change in monkey D is a decrease, opposite to the increase of the DBS animals.
deviations: The paper reports no test for monkey D; the criterion applies the Methods' ANOVA to its bins.

outcomes.notes: With the Fig2A script's model (monkey, and PrePost, side and tract with all their interactions; type III), PrePost x side F(1,3187) = 4.64, P = 0.031, partial eta squared 0.0015. outcomes.notes: Under the amended criterion, the paper's Fig. 4 script's test (rank-sum of each ROI's 122 off-diagonal changes against 122 zeros, significant at P < 0.05/123), computed as MATLAB's ranksum (tie and continuity corrected), gives 69 ROIs for the DBS group (41 of 54 cortical, 28 of 69 subcortical) and 44 for the controls, the reported counts, with or without the diagonal. The largest P counted is 3.88e-04 in both groups, the largest value listed in Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 (3.9e-4). Of the variants, the same test at the Methods' threshold 0.01/123 gives 62 and 36, the pre against post rank-sum 10 to 44 (DBS) and 4 to 15 (controls), and the signed-rank of the changes 60 to 85 and 27 to 49. What the answer changed. The earlier criterion named only the pre against post rank-sum and the signed-rank, at 0.01/122 or 0.01, none of which puts both counts in tolerance, so the outcome rested on an assumption that the script's test and threshold are the paper's (reproduced, assumed). The reader's answer of 2026-11-03 (questions/001773.yaml) made the script's test and threshold the criterion and changed the statement's 122 ROIs to 123. The outcome stays reproduced, the counts are the same, and it no longer rests on an assumption.
deviations: The matrices have 123 ROIs, so each ROI has 122 values, the n of the legend; the threshold uses 123 as the script and the amended criterion do (0.01/122 is also shown).

findings.statement: The Data availability statement says the functional MRI data are deposited in this dandiset, but it holds only derived values (seed connectivity of the voxels of 17 target ROIs for monkeys N, T and D, and three group-average connectomes). There are no fMRI or DWI images, no whole-brain seed maps, no seed connectivity for the nonsurgical controls B, W and H, and no per-monkey connectomes, so the voxelwise cluster maps of Fig. 5a, Fig. 6d and Extended Data Figs. 7, 8 and 10d cannot be tested.

The connectomes in "Source Data FC matrix.xlsx" (123 x 123) carry no ROI names. The Fig. 4 script reads them from atlas key and reorder files (CHARM_key_4.txt, SARM_key_4.txt, reorder_rois.txt) that are not deposited, so no ROI can be named and the network sorting of Fig. 4c cannot be repeated.

The legend in dbs_behavior_data_a.xlsx codes foraging as yes 2 and no 1, but every foraging value is 0 or 1; read as 1 yes, the values give the paper's statistics. The same legend gives group codes 1 (DBS) and 0 (non-stimulation control), while monkey D's rows carry group 2.

In CC1_MCC_CB_data_a.xlsx two fields of monkey T's control side (section T423, fields 3 and 4) carry CC1/DAPI ratios that do not match their counts (44.9 and 35.4 % against 35.4 and 44.2 % from the counts); field 4's ratio is field 3's. Two MCC-CB fields have more CC1-positive than DAPI-positive cells (ratio above 100 %). The paper's script uses the ratio column; with the ratio from the counts the side effect changes from F = 9.00 to 9.03.

In dbs_EMgratio_MCC_CB_data_a.xlsx the column headed "diameter of axon(pixel)" holds half the mean of the long and short diameters (a radius), and "diameter of axon(nm)" the same in nm. The g-ratio column is consistent with the Methods' definition.

The Fig. 4 script counts an ROI as changed when `ranksum` of its changes against a vector of zeros gives P < 0.05/nrois (nrois = 123), while the Methods and the Fig. 4b legend give a rank-sum test at "P < 0.01 with Bonferroni correction". The script's threshold reproduces the 69 and 44 ROIs of Supplementary Tables 1 and 2, whose largest listed P is 3.9e-4, above 0.01/122.
The Fig. 6a legend gives the PrePost x side x tract interaction as F(1,1238) = 6.02, P = 0.0025. The data give F = 6.02 and P = 0.0025 with 2 numerator df, as three tracts imply.

For fig6e-monkey-d-no-network-reduction, the paper does not say whether "the widespread reductions ... were not observed" in monkey D covers the control hemisphere. Its own Fig. 6e legend lists a significant control-side CEN difference, which the data show to be a decrease (P = 0.0089). The Methods list LIM without area 25, while the script and the legend's voxel counts include it. The authors could say which hemisphere the sentence refers to.

The dandiset's metadata names the paper only in its title, with no related resource, and gives no species, approach, measurement technique or variables measured. The sheets have no data dictionary beyond the legends inside some of them.

The seed connectivity tables hold one value per voxel and session, and the file names say "concatenated". The paper does not say whether a session's seed map was computed on concatenated runs or averaged over per-run maps, and no per-run maps are deposited.
The FigE1 script computes the foraging standard errors from column 2, the movement column (lines 91 to 96), so the error bars of the foraging plot in Extended Data Fig. 1 are those of movement.

Two scripts are deposited twice under two names with identical text (`Fig4 Fujimoto_NatNeuro_2026_FCmatrix.m` and `Fig4andE10C_Fujimoto_NatNeuro_2026_FCmatrix.m`; `Fig6DandE10D_dbs_FC_25norm_mkD_analysisscript_a.m` and `Fig6DandE10Ddbs_FC_25norm_mkD_analysisscript_a.m`).

entries.title: White matter and network changes after subcallosal cingulate DBS in macaques (Fujimoto et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fujimoto, Fujimoto, Elorette et al. (2026) on dandiset 001785, which holds per-session FA maps and normalized seed connectivity maps of two stimulated monkeys, one implanted control and three nonsurgical controls, with CC1 and DAPI immunofluorescence images and electron micrographs. Tract and ROI membership of voxels is taken from the paper's source data in DANDI:001773, and cells are counted from the images. The connectivity matrices and the hand-measured g-ratios cannot be tested from the dandiset.
